title.purpose: Page heading, and the strip title on an incident page.

lead.purpose: First statement of a section: verdict, summary, the day's spend. The wordmark at weight 700.

body.purpose: Running text, capped at 70ch. Tabular numerals are on page-wide.

strip-title.purpose: The title of a strip on the board, one line.

entry.purpose: The value in a cell and the text of a record row. Weight 500 in pen. A literal 0.875rem in the stylesheet, not a custom property.

small.purpose: Standing lines, facts, notes, navigation, buttons, tables. --t-small.

heading-label.purpose: Uppercase bay names and section headings over a 2px ink rule.

label.purpose: Uppercase cell labels, column heads, record tags, flags, the stage line. --t-label, tracking 0.04em to 0.06em.

holder-id.purpose: The incident number in the holder. The severity word under it is sans 700 at 0.625rem, uppercase.

figure.purpose: Counts, costs and table cells in monospace.

meta.purpose: Times, event kinds, payloads. A literal 0.75rem in the stylesheet, not a custom property.

colorSchemes.note: Each CSS custom property has one light and one dark value. Frontmatter keys ending in -dark are the dark value of the same variable. A print palette puts strips on white (#ffffff) with a #eef1ef well and the light inks.

insetFrames.name: resolved-holder-frame
insetFrames.purpose: The severity colour kept as a frame on a resolved strip. A frame, not elevation.

insetFrames.name: target-row-ring
insetFrames.purpose: The record row a citation points to.

focus.name: focus
focus.purpose: Every focusable element. On a board strip the outline surrounds the whole strip.

motion.name: strip-slide
motion.purpose: A strip sliding between bays on live refresh, as a view transition. Names are set per strip from script through the CSSOM. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: board-crossfade
motion.purpose: Cross-fade of the rest of the page during the same view transition.

motion.name: state-ease
motion.purpose: Colour changes on hover and press (navigation, buttons, chips, strip border). State feedback, not movement.

motion.name: refresh-interval
motion.purpose: The board refetches itself; paused while the tab is hidden or focus is on the board.

motion.name: changed-offset
motion.purpose: A changed strip stands out of line, with no transition, until pointed at, pressed or focused.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 1.5rem, bar on one line, board in two columns, full table columns.

breakpoints.name: desk
breakpoints.purpose: Board in four columns, wells at least 60vh.

delivery.contentSecurityPolicy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
delivery.note: No inline style or script, no other host. Meter widths are SVG attributes; view-transition names are set from script through the CSSOM.

narrative.overview:
The console is an air traffic control strip board. The ground is a grey-green rack. An incident is an off-white printed strip in a holder, ruled into labelled boxes. A bay is a stage of the pipeline: Triage, Investigation, Open, Resolved. Where a strip sits says what it is waiting for, so the board answers "where does everything stand" before a word is read.

Everything on a strip is either printed or written in pen. Printed ink is what code recorded. Pen blue, slanted, is what a model said. The operator reads the model's words as annotation and never as fact, then opens the strip and finds each claim tied to the tool call behind it. The system is flat and dense: hairlines, square corners, no shadow, no gradient, no picture. It is the opposite of the dark observability dashboard of stat tiles over a table, which this world refuses.

The console is server-rendered and makes no request to another host. That constraint shapes the look as much as the metaphor does: system fonts only, one stylesheet, one small script, no inline style anywhere.
keyCharacteristics: A rack, bays and strips: position carries state.
Two voices, one rule everywhere: printed ink for code, blue italic for a model.
Severity is the fill of the holder, and is always also written as a word.
Hairlines and square corners; depth comes from three flat tones (rack, well, strip).
Small uppercase labels over plain values, figures in monospace with tabular numerals.
Light and dark follow the system setting; a print palette puts the strips on white paper.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: What code recorded is printed ink, upright. What a model said is pen blue and italic. One rule on every page: a verdict, a summary, a claim, a suggested step are pen; a fact about a model call (its tokens, cost, duration, failure) is printed ink. The slant means the voice never rests on colour alone.

rules.name: The Reversed Tag Rule
rules.body: A tag reversed out of solid ink marks what left the server (a notification that was sent), and nothing else. A tag for anything that stayed inside is plain or outlined.

rules.name: The Written Severity Rule
rules.body: Severity lives in the fill of the holder and is always also written there as a word (critical, warning, info, unknown). Severity colour is never used for text, borders of other parts, or decoration.

rules.name: The Turned Over Rule
rules.body: A resolved strip keeps its severity colour as a 3px frame inside the holder, with a clear ground and printed ink. The colour says what it was; the empty holder says it is over.

rules.name: The Same Host Rule
rules.body: System fonts only. The pages load nothing from another host, so no webfont is ever added, whether hosted elsewhere or bundled.

rules.name: The Counted In Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for what is counted or cited: ids, counts, costs, times, event kinds, payloads. A sentence is never set in it.

rules.name: The Fixed Form Rule
rules.body: On the board a strip is six boxes, one line each, always the same height. Reasons and long values belong to the incident page, not to the board.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by tone and a 1px line. No drop shadow, no blur, no gradient, no translucent layer.

dos: Do set every word a model produced in pen blue italic, and every fact code recorded in upright printed ink, on every page.
Do write severity as a word in the holder whenever the holder is filled or framed with its colour.
Do keep the reversed ink tag for what left the server.
Do build new surfaces from the strip ground with a 1px edge hairline and 1px rule hairlines inside, corners square.
Do label every box with a small uppercase label and put the value under it in plain type.
Do set ids, counts, costs, times and event kinds in monospace.
Do say what was not done in a printed line: a stage that is off, a call that failed, a budget that is spent, a claim with no tool call behind it.
Do keep interactive targets at 2.75rem tall for buttons, fields and navigation.
Do set per-element values without inline style: SVG attributes for meters, the CSSOM from script for view-transition names.
Do define every new colour for light and dark together, and check the print palette.
donts: Don't use pen blue for anything code recorded, or use italic for emphasis: the slant belongs to the model.
Don't use a severity colour outside a holder, or let colour be the only sign of severity.
Don't reverse a tag for anything that stayed on the server; the changed tag is outlined.
Don't add a shadow, a gradient, a blur or a rounded corner.
Don't load a font, script, image or style from another host, and don't add a webfont.
Don't write a `style` attribute or a `<style>` block: the content policy refuses them.
Don't let a strip on the board grow: no wrapped title, no seventh box, no reason text.
Don't add a second motion. A strip sliding between bays is the only movement, and it is off under reduced motion.
Don't build the dashboard of stat tiles over a table.
Don't show approvals, actions or autonomy controls as if they existed.
